excerpt: A long-form thesis on financial theory and a new asset class: what makes a movement succeed, where movements fail, and why SPX6900 may be the Ultimate Movement Asset.
body:
This article will explore financial theory and discuss a new asset class. It will assume you are not familiar with what SPX6900 is and will present evidence on why you should research it. This is not financial or investment advice, but one coin is enough so what do you have to lose. 1 SPX6900 token is equal to about $0.37 United States dollars today. Enough price talk. Onward.

The Thesis:

The greatest potential ROI in history is standing right in front of us. A worldwide movement with no borders, barriers to entry, or institutional oversight that can stop it that you can invest in. The first asset in history with no ceiling, as the more it grows, the more desirable it is to be a part of, and the stronger its power becomes. The first truly reflexive asset is a movement asset. The Ultimate Movement Asset. I will attempt to describe to you why I believe this.

Definitions:

· Ultimate Movement Asset: the theoretical, most complete version of a movement asset — one that satisfies every trait a movement needs to succeed while avoiding the failure points that cause most movements (and most crypto assets) to collapse.

· Reflexive / Reflexivity: a feedback loop where a rising price makes the underlying story more believable, which attracts more belief and drives the price higher still — the same loop can work in reverse.

· Memecoin: a cryptocurrency created around a joke, meme, or cultural reference rather than a stated business use case, whose value is driven mostly or entirely by community and attention rather than revenue or utility.

· Decentralized rails: the underlying blockchain infrastructure a token runs on that isn't owned or controlled by a single company, bank, or government, so no central party can freeze, halt, or reverse transactions.

· TAM (Total Addressable Market): the maximum number of people or dollars a given asset, product, or idea could possibly reach if it succeeded completely.

· SPX6900 (SPX): the decentralized cryptocurrency this article uses as its central case study for the Ultimate Movement Asset, explored in full later in this piece.

· Aeons: the name SPX6900's holders and community members use to refer to themselves. The word Aeon also generally refers to an immeasurably long or indefinite period of time.

· DCA (Dollar-Cost Averaging): investing a fixed or arbitrary amount at regular intervals regardless of price, rather than trying to time the market.

· Fixed supply: a total token count that is capped permanently and can never be increased, unlike company stock (which can issue new shares) or fiat currency (which can be printed).

Throughout this thesis, I’ll track what I believe defines the Ultimate Movement Asset. Essentially piecing together what I present into the core themes of the most ideal asset. Later, I will help you connect the dots for yourself. Come along for the ride.

What Makes a Good Movement[[Q]]

Dream and Purpose:

Something worth fighting for: A dream is the seed every real movement grows from — a shared vision of a better world that gives otherwise disconnected people a reason to believe in the same thing at the same time and connect with one another. Without a dream, a movement is just speculation with extra steps; with one, it has something worth organizing around long after the initial wave of excitement fades.

Something’s broken and needs fixing: This type of purpose gives a movement its Schelling point – a reason people join without thinking twice. Today, some examples of what’s broken and needs fixing include the cost-of-living crisis, the loneliness epidemic, and a K-shaped economy: problems that touch nearly everyone, regardless of where you come from or what you do for a living. A movement built around fixing these starts with an edge most others don't have.

The majority is losing to the minority: And this one is big. This is a tipping point measure, statistical proof that the controversial or unaccepted idea like going against the status quo can come to fruition because enough people can agree in theory. Wealth concentration, wage stagnation against asset prices, the shrinking of the middle class – these aren't just feelings, they're documented, which is what makes the current world’s ground so fertile for a movement to take root.

From this, I’d argue:

~ The Ultimate Movement Asset will have a dream and purpose attached to it so powerful that much of the world will understand and resonate with eventually. ~

Collective Behaviors:

To achieve a purpose-driven movement, the people within the movement must develop collective behaviors in a way that is coordinating. This is proven throughout history as a MUST for cultures and movements that stick around or are successful. Christians collectively attend Church and pray every Sunday. Sports teams collectively work out and practice daily to achieve their goals together. Book groups collectively read their books and then convene to discuss on a routine basis. In order to develop a meaning in a movement or activity with others, the movement must have collective behaviors that are followed. The only way to organize mass numbers of different minds is to train the same way.

From this, I’d argue:

~ The Ultimate Movement Asset will possess collective behaviors across the people participating, creating an inseparable group of like-minded individuals. ~

Social Stickiness:

If people have a belief, vision, or dream, they have a purpose in chasing that belief, vision, or dream, and they develop collective behaviors to achieve that dream and live their lives in a way that services that purpose, there needs to be some sort of social stickiness – what if things start to go wrong[[Q]] Who sticks around and doesn’t abandon their dream or purpose and why do they do so[[Q]] If there really is something worth fighting for, if there is a deep driving purpose wrapped into a movement, people will fight for it. The test for this is time. The longer a vision is fought for, the deeper the meaning must go.

If you want to find something easy to believe in, look for something that’s been around for a while. If you want to find something that will stick around for a long time and become that “easy to believe in” thing, look for deep meaning that the broader population hasn’t discovered yet, as well as some beginning form of validation in the test-of-time.

From this, I’d argue:

~ The Ultimate Movement Asset will have a deep driving purpose that fuels its culture and builds a true long lasting social stickiness. ~

Lateral Ownership vs. Vertical Ownership:

A large part of the social stickiness discussion is also rooted in lateral ownership vs vertical ownership. When I describe these two just think of it as a company hierarchy vs. you and your friends. A company’s hierarchy is vertical ownership: the CEO or Founder owns the company, the people “below” them manage others in the business, the people “below” them do the dirty work, etc. etc. in a vertical distribution of power. You and your friends typically represent lateral ownership, where you would describe to an outsider your friend group or your friends, but there is no direct leader or owner. You are all “laterally” owners of your friend group. My friend group is no more mine than it is my friends’.

Lateral ownership is incredibly hard to develop from scratch and takes a lot of time but is infinitely more robust than vertical ownership. If the top of the pyramid messes up in a vertically owned organization, expect the whole thing to come crashing down. I’ve witnessed this repeatedly in the NFT market since 2020 – where a collection is launched promising this this and that, delivers on very few of their promises (sometimes only even missing one expectation), and collapses.

In a laterally owned organization, there is no top of the pyramid. There are of course louder voices than others, more trusted voices, and more tenured voices that can lead to inner invisible hierarchies, however, they can be replaced at zero cost to the broader group. This is the flexibility and sustainability a laterally owned group has. For a movement to be truly sustainable, it must be laterally owned.

From this, I’d argue:

~ The Ultimate Movement Asset will be built on lateral ownership, as it is more robust and carries less risk than vertically owned movements. ~

Effective in Communicating a Vision to Others:

Even if you have a belief, a vision, a purpose, are developing collective behaviors, have social stickiness, and have a laterally owned movement, the dream and purpose can’t develop into a full-blown movement until its participants are effective in communicating their vision to outsiders. I believe the easiest way today to begin a real robust and developing movement is online and on social media. The highest-powered marketing machine in this day and age is a swarm of people creating content for their cause, like I am doing here. It’s about giving people a reason to use their creativity for a greater purpose.

The reason this is so powerful is twofold: On one hand, a swarm of people that care about something so much as to put their creativity and time into it is fundamentally a marketing team with a $0 budget and unlimited work product. Technically infinite ROI on marketing. On the other hand, it shows others that this idea or movement is so powerful that I spent weeks writing a 19-page research paper on why you should look into it. The movement has true meaning to people that are a part of it, and that is reason enough to investigate what they are talking about. I believe this is a new and not very well understood means of communication that allows an idea to permeate through society at its own pace and will naturally grow if it is worth it.

From this, I’d argue:

~ The Ultimate Movement Asset will be naturally built on social media and internet native rails via a “swarm” of people who care, as this is the most effective and sustainable way to market an idea. ~

What Issues Can Movements Face[[Q]]

Single Point of Failure:

“Management team”

“Founder of the project”

“Leadership team”

“Dev”

“Brokerage”

When the risk is concentrated on one entity attempting to develop a movement specifically, it is almost guaranteed to fail. Failure in this sense is not achieving its “full potential” (or whatever the generally agreed-upon full potential was), there can be a wave of success within a movement, but it can still fail at its ultimate goal. GameStop, as we’ll discuss later, had a massive wave of success in its movement to squeeze the hedge funds and catch them red-handed, and in the end the hedge funds themselves turned off the buy button, ending the movement. The US-only brokerage exchanges were the single point of failure here. A single point of failure can be more than just the “Dev” or CEO or whoever. It can be the rails the movement is built upon.

From this, I’d argue:

~ The Ultimate Movement Asset will live on decentralized rails with no centralization risk. It will also have no single point of leadership. ~

Short-Term Focus:

Anything with a short-term goal will have short term success. Play small games, win small prizes as they say. An important part of your investment journey should be to understand what timeframe you’re participating in. With 99% of memecoins, you’re playing in the 10-second to 10-minute timeframe. If you choose to participate, know that’s your window, and overstaying your welcome comes with consequences. This also implies there is a 1%. We’ll talk about that 1% soon.

Generally, most anything that would classify as a movement has some sort of long-term focus. Similarly with stocks, bonds, real estate, alternative assets, etc., the most valuable assets in each of those categories has a long-term focus. Apple, Nvidia, Microsoft, Google, Amazon, (each around $2T to $4T) all entirely forward looking and long-termist. U.S. Treasuries ($51T) all long-termist. Real Estate ($624T) all obviously long-termist. Private Equity ($7.5T) [[AMP]]amp; Hedge Funds ($5.7T) long-term investment period. Bitcoin ($1.3T) extremely long-termist. Each category leader also has its own respective goal in mind. The tech giants want to further the technology the world uses on a daily basis. The U.S. Treasuries want to back the lending of money indefinitely. Real Estate doesn’t need a long-term goal: people need houses, it’s a long-term necessity. PE [[AMP]]amp; Hedge Funds have a long-term goal of making their investors boatloads of cash, and operate toward achieving that goal sometimes at the cost of others.

From this, I’d argue:

~ The Ultimate Movement Asset will be long-termist and have a goal that supports its longevity. ~

(excuse the fact that I made up the word long-termist you get the idea its something that possesses long termism)

Small TAM:

TAM stands for Total Addressable Market. In other words: if this succeeds to its fullest, how many people are involved[[Q]] What is the maximum size of the market this could capture. For something like a baby toy business, the TAM is technically how many humans are between 0-4 years old at a given time. The TAM of a new basketball shoe design is the number of people that play basketball in the world plus those that just like to wear basketball shoes. It’s a measurement of how many lives can this particular thing actually touch. The greater the TAM, the higher the potential.

From this, I’d argue:

~ The Ultimate Movement Asset will have the largest TAM of any asset. Its TAM will essentially be everyone with an internet connection. ~

Cultural Difficulties:

A movement can’t just spawn out of nowhere either, it needs to be attached to a broader idea that lots of people agree with or can resonate with. As we just discussed, that broader idea needs to be able to encompass a large percentage of the world to be a movement that persists into a cultural phenomenon. Trying to create a TAM large enough to capture a majority of the world’s population is not easy either, especially with a financial movement. Let’s look at some examples of movements and or trends that are culturally specific.

MAGA: Make America Great Again is a political movement culturally tied to the United States. People living outside of the US have no reason to join, engage, or understand what MAGA is. Even so, it is present in a lot of United States citizens’ worlds. It is also inherently culturally dividing, as it is a current political party's mantra. A movement can be large in your bubble, and non-existent in someone else’s. (just an example, I don’t care what my or your political affiliation is)

K-Pop: More of a cultural phenomenon and an entertainment branch with exploding popularity. K-Pop is much more transnational than MAGA and can branch out to any part of the world but still has a cultural difficulty or barrier. It falls in the Anime / Eastern Asian culture bucket, which many people on earth have a hard time resonating with.

Brainrot Humor: Also more of a cultural phenomenon with Gen Z / Gen Alpha but nonetheless taking a large mindshare of the world. Instagram Reels and Tik Tok have generally popularized this type of humor, and it fundamentally changes people’s sense of humor. The cultural difficulties and barriers here are resonating with anyone who grew up in the ages before social media. Close to 70% of the world will never understand your brainrot humor.

From this, I’d argue:

~ The Ultimate Movement Asset will be culturally indifferent and will have no social boarders and no physical boarders. ~

What Are Some Examples of Financialized Movements [[AMP]]amp; Did They Work[[Q]]

GameStop:

GameStop was a beautiful glitch in the matrix. The first real time the little guy scared the sh*t out of the big guy in the broader free markets of today’s day and age. Roaring Kitty called out that GME had more shares being shorted than truly existed and there was a chance to liquidate the shorts to oblivion. He noticed crime that was going to fly under the radar as well as an opportunity for a massive squeeze and called it out until people finally listened to him when they ultimately realized he was right.

What unfolded was the stock appreciating from $2 per share to almost $500 per share, entirely driven off retail coordination [[AMP]]amp; the belief it would work.

The GameStop saga proved retail (the general population) can organize and send an asset to unbelievable heights. Something that gets overlooked massively is that the system (the 500) can also turn off the buy button in their own house. The vision was there, the belief was there, the community was there, the execution was there, and the institutions decided what the rules were. The solution here is to coordinate on decentralized financial rails, not in the S[[AMP]]amp;P500’s house.

Still, if there was a scenario where GME was on-chain, meaning you could buy it from a decentralized exchange and “turning off the buy button” becomes impossible, there’s another issue. A stock represents shares of ownership in a company. That company can issue new shares whenever they want, and it makes a lot more sense to issue new shares when the value is higher than usual. Your slice of the pie can and will be diluted in a stock-based movement.

I would also recommend you go check out @Cryptic_Mang 's presentation on this topic called “Movement Coins Save The Middle Class”, as he explains the GME phenomenon in much more detail than I do here.

From this, I’d argue:

~ The Ultimate Movement Asset will occur on decentralized rails with a fixed supply, as it will be uncensorable and non-dilutive. These properties give the Ultimate Movement Asset the freedom to continue for as long as those that believe keep believing. ~

Dogecoin:

Shortly after the GameStop saga, Dogecoin ripped from less than half a penny to 74 cents. Why[[Q]] Because the joke was that it did nothing. It’s just a dog coin and it can hit a dollar after being worth less than half a penny, that was it. Beautifully simple, easy enough to understand, and culturally backed by the richest man in the world, Elon Musk. “If we all buy it like we did GME, it can go parabolic”. The decentralized nature [[AMP]]amp; relative fixed supply at the time (inflates at roughly 5b tokens per year, so inflationary for sure, but no “stock issuances” at the peak per se) created an environment where something similar to GME could happen.

I would argue the underlying story with Doge wasn’t strong enough. You can’t push “its funny because it does nothing” long enough for it to gather a long-lasting critical mass of true believers. Was dogecoin a success[[Q]] YES. It absolutely achieved immense results and showed again what is possible when retail coordinates on decentralized rails. Was it the Ultimate Movement Asset[[Q]] Absolutely not. It will not stand the test of 10, 20, or 30 years when its supply is inflating with no maximum, and when the story people rally around is stuck in the past. The story must become reflexive: it must get stronger over time and with price appreciation.

From this, I’d argue:

~ The Ultimate Movement Asset will have a story that is reflexive and continues to grow uninterrupted due to its decentralization and fixed supply. ~

AI:

AI is the most current, most obvious form of a movement I’ve seen in a while. Yes, Claude, ChatGPT and Grok can do incredible things, and we’re unlocking a world that we’ve yet to live in – this is a real pivotal moment in history. However, as financial assets, Anthropic, OpenAI, and XAI are TERRIBLE on paper – Anthropic made its first dollars of profit last quarter (Q2, 2026) and are valued at around a Trillion dollars. Financially, this is only driven by the story around the asset, or the social movement in the world driving the value of their asset. My company talks about AI, your company talks about AI, your parents are using AI, it’s everywhere and changing the way we live right now. This is a prime example of a movement and it’s happening right in front of your eyes.

In fact, if we didn’t have any way to gauge Anthropic’s profitability at all, I’d imagine the story around AI could theoretically drive Anthropic’s value up with no ceiling, as people have never yet lived with AI. It’s so new and revolutionary and fantastic at what it does that it’s valued at a Trillion dollars before its first operating profit ever. I’d argue the value may even be constricted from the traditional finance measurements. How would you value an asset with such great societal meaning if it didn’t have Assets, Liabilities, Equities, or EBITDA[[Q]] We will see how AI as a whole plays out: which companies fail and which succeed, but I can say for certain the financial value of these companies is pure belief in the future, not earnings per share.

Bitcoin:

Of course, we have to touch on Bitcoin: the financial, cultural, social phenomenon of the 2010s [[AMP]]amp; 2020s. Bitcoin, unlike these other examples, emerged as an idea, not a company or industry. The idea was to solve the double spending problem that comes from deleting the middle man out of a transaction. If there was nobody there to verify the transaction, how would we know someone isn't spending fake money[[Q]] This is fundamentally what Bitcoin solves. It's a beautiful discovery and the product of what I'd imagine be years of theory by Satoshi. Bitcoin is my generation's wealth storing asset thanks to this discovery.

Bitcoin is direct validation that something with no promises, no leadership team, and no marketing team can become a trillion dollar asset. It's an idea who's place in this world is incredibly valuable. Even so, people try to value Bitcoin in a traditional way, which is nearly impossible. There's stock to flow models, technical analysis, cycle theory, and none of it ever explains Bitcoin's movements or development correctly. Separate from the Ultimate Movement Asset however, as Bitcoin does technically promise to provide utility value to society as a whole in the form of being the best decentralized way to transact and store value. If Bitcoin's technology is somehow topped in the future, and something else performs it's purpose better than Bitcoin does, it will render Bitcoin largely obsolete. In this view, Bitcoin's movement to create more sound money are technically dependent on it's fundamental structure being the best version of sound money we have on Earth. Today that holds true, in the future who knows. Regardless, Bitcoin clearly proves that an asset can hold tremendous value without having revenue, cash flows, or any traditional finance valuing methods.

From this, I’d argue:

~ The Ultimate Movement Asset does not need revenues, cash flows, or earnings to succeed, and will outperform assets that do have those traditional financial anchors as it will be difficult to value. ~

What is SPX6900[[Q]]

At Our Core:

We’re aiming to flip the stock market. Yes that’s right, to become more valuable than the S[[AMP]]amp;P 500, over $69T market cap at least. We believe the S[[AMP]]amp;P500, and symbolically the majority of systematic financial controllers in our current society have gotten too large, are not working in the public’s interest, and are generally siphoning wealth from the [[AMP]]gt;99% to the [[AMP]]lt;1%. We believe that social media has been over-engineered to steal your dopamine, trap you in, and sell you products rather than see your friends and be “social”. We believe “shrinkflation” is a serious issue, as at the fundamental, cultural, and symbolic level, it is companies squeezing every penny out of people who are trudging their way through the mud to even figure out how they’re going to pay for the product in the first place. We believe the governments of the world and the fundamental backbones of how societies operate are an integral piece of why this is possible and is happening. From a social and financial mobility lens, today's younger generation has it harder than their parents for the first time in recent recorded history.

We believe people were put on this earth to better our own lives and the lives of others, and the current zeitgeist of the world is so self-centered at the top, in the 1% of humans, where it really should be focused on the 99%. We believe there’s power in organizing together and rising up against this oppressive power of the world, and doing so in a non-violent, make-our-own-rules type of way. We choose to do this on decentralized rails, with a fixed supply, and with this lofty, unreasonable goal. We have built this in a way that can’t be attacked the way GME was or fizzle out the way Dogecoin has since 2021. We are ready to continue communicating our vision until it’s seen through and have created an asset structured to do so uninterrupted forever.

A Truly Neutral Culture Aimed at Enlightenment:

There are a few main mantras in SPX other than Flip the Stock Market. They are: “Stop Trading and Believe in Something”, “Persist Forever”, “Peaceful Life over Greed”, and “There is No Chart”. All were first spread from SPX6900, if you see these being used for other tokens or stocks, just know they came from the 2023 Aeons that chose to take SPX6900 seriously and build something real. These phrases embody and spread our culture to new potential holders, and here is why they’re so important.

- Stop Trading and Believe in Something

Here’s a fun fact for you: Roughly 96% of Pump Fun wallets (memecoin platform) either lost money or made less than $500 in profit since the platform came out (statistic from @CoinMarketCap on March 30, 2026). The oversaturation of dopamine spiking, moment-in-time coins have led to it being almost impossible to trade profitably let alone hold for more than a couple hours. Back in 2018 when there were 100 coins to choose from, your odds of picking the one were infinitely higher than they are today. Today there are around 37 million coins to choose from. The solution to this is to concentrate your focus on picking the one by finding the Ultimate Movement Asset.

- Persist Forever

Our unique asset gives us this choice. With stocks you can only persist as long as the company continues to live up to its expectations. With utility coins you can only persist as long as the dev team continues building up to expectations. With 99% of memecoins you can only persist as long as the meme is relevant, as most are tokenized moments in time. With SPX6900, you can persist until the stock market is flipped, and the “meme” of flipping the stock market is reflexive. The closer we get to flipping the market, the more real it becomes, and the more fuel it adds to the fire. This phenomenon doesn’t exist for any other asset. It’s based on collective belief, not revenue streams. This flips the script, and eventually the market.

- Peaceful Life Over Greed

One of the quieter mantras in the collective consciousness, but arguably my favorite. PLOG for short, we encourage all Aeons to live a peaceful life rather than being greedy, cynical, or a doomer. We’re developing a PvE asset, a movement that encourages 99% of humans to join us and develop a better world with stronger values (as opposed to a PvP asset, where your winning is another player losing). This comes from understanding what we hold, and knowing our best shot at victory is to continue as long as possible, which requires a tolerance to volatility, patience, and a peaceful mind regardless of what the market does. Living a peaceful life means knowing it will take time to unfold and believing in ourselves hard enough to not look at the charts, not stress over what’s going on in the markets, and to focus on our crafts, what makes us happy, and spending time with the people we love. The greatest wealth created in investing is from holding the right asset for a long enough period of time, and we believe PLOG is the best way to achieve this.

- There is No Chart

The most “annoying” mantra to outsiders who haven’t taken the time to dig deeper is There is No Chart. The purpose of this saying is to take the volatility dopamine out of our game. We don’t discuss the price moving up or down, reason being our focus is on developing our own lore, like I am doing here. People in SPX6900 are not questioning their conviction as they watch a -10% candle shoot down through their support lines, nor are they getting more validation on their conviction when they see a +20% candle upward. We treat it more binary in order to stay focused on the mission – “Is the stock market flipped[[Q]] No[[Q]] Continue persisting forever”.

No matter what the price of SPX is, Aeons continue building culture, lore, and collective understanding and belief while the rest of the market waits for their coins to get exciting again. The excitement is in the journey here. When you take the focus off the price of the asset and put it on the beautiful works of art people in the community are making, it turns the narrative away from volatility and emotional rollercoasters to truly building the foundation the price will ultimately be decided upon.

Flywheel of Validation:

This is something @realcryptocow talked about in his presentation “Grimm Economics”, which I highly recommend you go check out. Essentially, the idea is stories need time to validate themselves, and movements are no different. They go through cycles of excitement and boredom, and usually many crypto assets go through only one of these cycles before dying out. Beginning of the cycle is exciting, there’s a new idea here, people are buying into this vision, and there’s runway ahead – exciting news anticipated, near term date everyone’s looking forward to, etc.. Then the peak of the flywheel, whatever people were waiting for happens and it coincides with the peak of its perceived value at that time. And finally, the end of the cycle where things get boring, people leave, and the anticipation of the future is no longer as bright. That inflection point in the slide is where I'd argue we stand today.

Great assets use this flywheel as validation and fuel. The Ultimate Movement Asset will repeat the flywheel indefinitely. The more times an asset can successfully dig itself up from the inflection point, the more robust it is and the more meaning the mission has to its people. There’s a reason it never dies, and the light burns bright regardless of market action. This is what SPX6900 aims to achieve. It’s currently rounding the corner on its second -80% drop, and it’s clear to myself and everyone still here that it’s about to run back a third spin on the flywheel. We’re only bolstering the belief of future Aeons. The hard work is done in boring markets. The hard work is being done by us. We are the reason people will come back and the mission will grow further. It becomes easier to stomach on each subsequent repetition of the flywheel. The asset becomes more immune to the boring side of the flywheel on each completed cycle.

Long-Term Vision:

This is generally a difficult attribute to truly achieve. For a business it’s an easy value proposition: we expect Google Amazon and Apple to keep running the world for the foreseeable future, so our “long-term vision” includes these companies. I’d argue historically, Bitcoin has been the asset with the most ambitious long-term vision, being to overtake the innerworkings of our global financial system and replace gold and USD as the primary financial settlement layer and wealth storing asset. Companies and ideologies develop into these long-term assets and visions for the broader population over time, but someone had the delusional vision one day and never gave up.

Think back to 2012, when you were doing whatever it is you were up to in 2012. Imagine someone coming up to you, a family member, a friend, anyone, and telling you that Bitcoin will be the primary settlement layer and wealth storing asset someday, while at the time it’s price per coin was ranging between $0.50 and $5.00. You would call them delusional, insane, crazy, and likely would get them in touch with a financial advisor “before they lose it all”. Now snap back to today, July 2026, where the US government is developing rules and regulations in how we govern digital assets. Where there are nations and companies that are closing in on a 1% of total BTC supply owned individually. And where the value of Bitcoin bounces around near the largest companies in the world, and the largest assets in the world. The long-term, highly delusional vision is the only way to find and develop the next huge thing.

SPX6900 is an equally long term, more intriguing movement that likely resonates with more people than Bitcoin would. The cost of living crisis is getting exponentially worse in the United States, elsewhere it has accelerated quicker. Uncertainty [[AMP]]amp; fear over AI replacing jobs, if there is a need for human involvement in the future, and fear of diminishing IQ value is greater than ever. Inflation is back at +4% in the US, quietly, and the president is saying “the economy is great” where the growth is really coming from money printing. War is continuing in the middle east, something the people in the US don’t want and haven’t voted or had input on, our tax money just goes toward hundreds of billions of dollars of bombs and conflict that we didn’t agree on. All these issues can be felt by people around the globe as well. SPX6900 combats ALL these issues simultaneously. It is a monetary protest over this control, a call to action calling out the systems that have gotten to this point. A satire of the 500 companies that are ruining our livelihoods on the margins. Calling out the absurdity of trusting the economies of the world that are inherently just stories themselves and are not working at the deepest level to better the lives of majority of people on earth. This is what we’re fighting for. We will be an equally compelling and investable story that instead works toward the betterment of society and the general population’s livelihoods. I truly believe we can achieve this.

Impossible to Stop Fundamentally:

Unlike GameStop, you cannot turn off the buy button on SPX6900. Sure, an exchange could stop you from buying from them in theory, but you can just buy from a different one. It is the most distributed crypto token on the market, you’re not getting a -50% 5-minute candle ever, I can promise due to the decentralization [[AMP]]amp; distribution. Unlike holding a stock, we cannot be diluted. There’s a fixed supply of SPX6900 tokens and no more can ever be created. Unlike Doge, SPX6900 has a reflexive narrative that will only add fuel to the fire as the asset grows in value. The closer we get to flipping the stock market, the more real it becomes, the less delusional it sounds, and the more “trustworthy” it is to new investors.
